title: SARATHI: Efficient LLM Inference by Piggybacking Decodes with Chunked Prefills
technique: chunked prefills + decode-maximal batching (one prefill chunk plus decodes per batch); uniform micro-batches for pipeline parallelism

optimized_metrics.evidence: a chunk size can be chosen such that the end-to-end throughput of the model is maximized
creating such uniform and compute-intensive batches ensures high GPU utilization throughout, as well as, minimizes pipeline bubbles in multi-GPU deployments
creating such uniform and compute-intensive batches ensures high GPU utilization throughout, as well as, minimizes pipeline bubbles in multi-GPU deployments

headline_claim.text: For the LLaMA-13B model on A6000 GPU, SARATHI improves decode throughput by up to 10x, and accelerates end-to-end throughput by up to 1.33x. ... When used with pipeline parallelism on GPT-3, SARATHI reduces bubbles by 6.29x, resulting in an end-to-end throughput improvement of 1.91x.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: decode phase throughput that we calculate based on the average time spent on decoding one token. For the baseline system, we compute the average decode time per token by dividing the time to process one decode iteration by the batch size.
metric_definitions.notes: decode-only throughput; in SARATHI the time of piggybacked decodes is isolated from the prefill chunk cost

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define this as the sum of bubble time for all the micro-batches across all iterations for a given request.
(not defined explicitly) end-to-end throughput of the model
metric_definitions.notes: never formally defined; measured on offline batches at fixed P:D ratio and sequence length; token units (input+output) implied, per single GPU/deployment

load_regime: offline fixed batch (batch size, P:D ratio, sequence length swept); pipeline experiment is simulated 10K requests, Zipf lengths
tradeoff_acknowledged: smaller chunks lower prefill arithmetic intensity and add KV re-read overhead, reducing efficiency; no latency (TTFT/TBT) trade-off analysed
workloads: synthetic: fixed seq length 1K-4K, P:D ratios 1-100, Zipf in simulation
extractor_notes: Early version of Sarathi: no TTFT/TBT/latency percentiles and no SLOs; objective is throughput only. 'End-to-end throughput' and 'decode throughput' used without token-unit definition. Pipeline-bubble time is an unusual metric.
